items.title: Players Eligible For In-Season Veteran Extensions In 2026/27
items.summary: As we explain in our glossary entry on veteran contract extensions, rookie scale extensions used to be the most common form of contract extension in the NBA. However, recent Collective Bargaining Agreements have loosened the rules on eligibility for veteran extensions and made them more financially advantageous, especially for players who don’t expect mega-deals. As a result, we’ve seen a substantial bump in veteran contract extensions in recent seasons. In every league year since 2021/22, at least 17 players have signed veteran extensions, including 20 in 2025/26. We’re not quite up to 17 yet in ’26/27, but there’s plenty of time for this season’s list to continue to grow, right up until June 30, 2027. items.title: NBA Europe Likely Aiming For ‘Soft Launch’ Next Fall
items.summary: The NBA’s aim to start a European league next fall could be a “soft launch” at best, considering the league doesn’t have any teams yet, The Athletic’s Joe Vardon reports. The NBA has partnered with FIBA as it looks to establish its own European league, tentatively known as NBA Europe. “Broadly speaking, it is implausible that a serious league could be launched (by next October),” a member of one potential NBA Europe franchise ownership group told Vardon. NBA commissioner Adam Silver expressed confidence last month that the new league would move forward, even though negotiations with the existing EuroLeague hit a snag. There’s still no clear resolution, according to Vardon, nor are there any formal agreements in place with the soccer conglomerates, private equity chiefs, and tech giants needed to form new teams in Europe’s largest markets.
